title: Coherent base change for invertible sheaves
statement:
Let $C/k$ be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, let $T$
be a locally Noetherian $k$-scheme, write $f_T:C_T=C\times_kT\to T$, and
let $\cL$ be invertible on $C_T$. Then $Rf_{T,*}\cL$ is locally
represented by a bounded complex of finite locally free
$\cO_T$-modules. For any $a:T'\to T$, its derived pullback is
canonically $Rf_{T',*}\cL_{T'}$. The locus where this complex is an
invertible module in degree $0$ is open; there $f_{T,*}\cL$ is
invertible, its formation commutes with arbitrary base change, and
$R^1f_{T,*}\cL=0$.

For an arbitrary test scheme $T$, the same open locus is obtained locally
by descending the finitely presented line bundle to a finitely generated
$k$-algebra and pulling back; the derived base-change isomorphism makes
the result independent of the chosen model.

*General form.* The detailed nodes prove this in the following
generality (the case $i=0$, $r=1$, $\cF=\cL$ is the lemma). Let
$f:X\to T$ be proper of finite presentation and $\cF$ an
$\cO_X$-module of finite presentation, flat over $T$; fix $i\in\Z$ and
$r\ge0$ and write $h^q(t):=\dim_{\kappa(t)}H^q(X_t,\cF_t)$.
The locus

$$
U_{i,\le r}:=\{t\in T:\ h^q(t)=0\ \text{for all }q\neq i\ \text{and}\ h^i(t)\le r\}
$$

is *open* in $T$, and over it $Rf_*\cF$ is, Zariski locally on
$U_{i,\le r}$, isomorphic to a finite free module placed in degree $i$,
of rank $h^i(t)$, its formation commuting with every base change
$T'\to U_{i,\le r}$. Consequently $h^i$ is locally constant on
$U_{i,\le r}$, the locus

$$
U_{i,r}:=\{t\in T:\ h^q(t)=0\ \text{for all }q\neq i\ \text{and}\ h^i(t)=r\}
$$

is open as well, and on $U_{i,r}$ one has $R^qf_*\cF=0$ for $q\neq i$,
$R^if_*\cF$ finite locally free of rank $r$, and the base-change maps of
[sk-thm-picard-semicon] are isomorphisms; a morphism $T'\to T$
factors through $U_{i,r}$ if and only if $Rf_{T',*}\cF_{T'}$ is
isomorphic to a finite locally free $\cO_{T'}$-module of rank $r$
placed in degree $i$. No reducedness of $T$ is needed.

proof.text: For the curve statement, base change of the projective morphism C→Spec(k) is proper and of finite presentation, and an invertible sheaf on C_T is finitely presented and flat over T. Applying [sk-thm-picard-coherence](a) gives, locally on T, a bounded complex K of finite free O_T-modules representing Rf_{T,*}𝓛, with the canonical derived pullback identification La^*Rf_{T,*}𝓛 ≃ Rf_{T′,*}𝓛_{T′} for every a:T′→T. The rank-one degree-zero locus is the case i=0,r=1 of the fixed-degree perfect-locus criterion [lem-pc-perfect-locus] (equivalently the open rank-locus of [lem-pc-flat-rf-open]); on it the complex is an invertible module in degree 0, so f_{T,*}𝓛 is invertible, R¹f_{T,*}𝓛=0, and taking cohomology of the derived pullback identification gives arbitrary base-change isomorphisms. This applies after descending a finitely presented line bundle to a finitely generated k-algebra, and the canonical derived base-change identification makes the resulting open independent of the chosen model.

source.place: Proof, “The lemma from the general form”

proof.text: For the general form, [sk-thm-picard-coherence](a) supplies on an affine neighbourhood a bounded complex K=[K^a→⋯→K^b] of finite free modules whose formation commutes with every base change and whose fibre cohomology is H^q(X_t,𝓕_t). By [sk-thm-picard-semicon], each fibre dimension h^q is upper semicontinuous; because K is bounded, only finitely many q occur locally. Hence the conditions h^q=0 for q≠i and h^i≤r define an open locus U_{i,≤r}. At a point of this locus, the fibre complex is exact away from i. The standard finite-free cancellation criterion encoded by [lem-pc-perfect-locus] removes split surjective end differentials and split injective beginning differentials, compatibly after shrinking the base, until K is a single finite free module M in degree i. Thus Rf_*𝓕 is locally M[-i], its formation commutes with every base change, h^i is locally constant, and the exact-rank locus U_{i,r} is open in U_{i,≤r}; on it R^qf_*𝓕=0 for q≠i, R^if_*𝓕 is finite locally free of rank r, and the cohomological base-change maps are isomorphisms because they are induced by the canonical derived base-change isomorphism of coherence.

For a morphism a:T′→T, if Rf_{T′,*}𝓕_{T′} is a finite locally free module of rank r placed in degree i, then every geometric fibre has h^q=r·δ_{q,i}; field extension preserves these dimensions, so the image lies in U_{i,r} and a factors through that open. Conversely, over U_{i,r} the local description from the preceding step and the canonical derived base-change isomorphism give the required finite locally free complex in degree i after every base change. This is also the functorial characterization in [lem-pc-flat-rf-open], and it shows that no reducedness assumption is needed.
